display.title: The Haggadah Explained in Yiddish, Part 1: Setting the Seder Table to Mah Nishtanah
display.summary_short: A Yiddish Haggadah class for children: how to set the Seder table and seder plate, then Kadesh, Urchatz, Karpas, Yachatz, Ha Lachma Anya and the Four Questions.
display.summary_long: Told in Yiddish for children, this is the first of three classes walking through the Pesach Seder step by step. The teacher begins with coming home from shul and setting the table: three matzos called Kohen, Levi and Yisroel, and the six items of the seder plate arranged in two segol shapes. He sings the order of the Seder, Kadesh Urchatz, and explains each step: making Kiddush right away so the children stay awake for the Four Questions, the special Havdalah when the Seder falls on Motzaei Shabbos, leaning to the left while drinking, washing for Urchatz without a brachah because of the wet karpas, having the maror in mind with the karpas brachah, and breaking the middle matzah for the afikoman. In Maggid he explains why matzah is 'poor man's bread' and the invitation and prayer of Ha Lachma Anya. He then explains why the child must ask, goes through the Four Questions one by one, recites Mah Nishtanah together twice, and stops as the father uncovers the matzah to answer with Avadim Hayinu.
display.lesson: The Seder is done in a set order so that children ask and parents answer; every detail on the table is there to teach about the Exodus.
